messages.subject: Re: [BioGeoBEARS] Re: Rexpokit removed from CRAN
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

Apologies for this difficulty!  I have many times in previous years done minor updates to rexpokit to keep it on CRAN, but I don't recall receiving anything this time.  It is always some tiny modification to the FORTRAN code to meet the every-changing standards of the CRAN gods.

But because of this possibility I have regularly archived the binaries (which are pre-compiled) on this GitHub:
https://github.com/nmatzke/Matzke_R_binaries

I did the last binary archive quite recently, so I imagine it would install easily on all machines...you can see Windows and Mac binaries available:

https://github.com/nmatzke/Matzke_R_binaries/tree/master/rexpokit

One note: I have had the experience where a whole lab class hits a GitHub page at once, and GitHub decides it's a Denial of Service attack and blocks the lab's IP address for 30 minutes. So it is best to make a local copy, e.g. on the course Canvas page or some such.

PS Another option is to try to install from the source code, which involves compiling the source code with gcc and gfortran.  On linux and macs this might work OK sometimes, but this would be a nightmare in a computer lab or on diverse student machines, especially Windows.  gcc and gfortran are nontrivial to install -- it can take hours and involve carefully checking various executable program locations etc.

(packages that are "pure R", like BioGeoBEARS, install easily from source as no compilation is needed, but installing rexpokit from the GitHub source code, rather than the GitHub precompiled binary archive, will have the same issue of needing compilation.  Use the precompiled binary archive if at all possible.

I will work on getting rexpokit back on CRAN but it won't happen until next week at the earliest.

Cheers,
Nick
